question: Does a project whose SVG was converted to a raster by the previous version still build the model it always built?
fixture: legacy-converted-svg.arch-project.zip, built by the Codex seat with the 7be8248f code: ingest plus one convert, packaged through that version's own snapshot and manifest API.
storedPixels: Mirrored, and visibly so: the source canvas of the opened project shows the F upside down with the blue square at the bottom right (legacy-converted-source-canvas-1440.png). That is what the old renderer wrote, and it is the project data.
marker: source.metadata.preview.frame = {kind:'manufacturing-bounds', leftMm:0, topMm:45, widthMm:45, heightMm:45, yDirection:'down'} with no sourceAxis, which is how a render from before the fix is recognised.

measured.blueSquareY_after_this_fix: +11.25 to +18 mm (Hub, live through the interface, STL read back with the Python standard library)

method: Open the package in the running application, approve the pending colour separation and the three-region source update, build, export the STL zip, read each slot back and take an area-weighted centroid and bounds.
verdict: The saved project builds what it always built. Its source canvas still shows the pixels it stored, which is its data, not the build.
